title: Manager Service Operations & AI
description: Ben jij een ervaren IT Operations Manager die niet alleen een supportorganisatie kan aansturen, maar ook kansen ziet om dienstverlening slimmer en efficiënter te maken met AI? Dan hebben wij een interessante uitdaging voor je. Voor Fivespark, een ambitieuze Managed Service Provider in Amstelveen, zoeken wij een Manager Service Operations & AI. In deze veelzijdige functie combineer je operationeel leiderschap met procesverbetering, automatisering en de verdere ontwikkeling van een eigen AI-agent. Je krijgt de verantwoordelijkheid over een team van 12 supportprofessionals én speelt een belangrijke rol in de transformatie naar een steeds verder geautomatiseerde IT-dienstverlening. Over Fivespark Fivespark is een innovatieve Managed Service Provider die bedrijven en overheden ondersteunt met moderne IT-oplossingen. De organisatie werkt aan de Managed Service Provider van de toekomst, waarin automatisering, kunstmatige intelligentie en datagedreven processen een steeds grotere rol spelen. Een belangrijk onderdeel hiervan is Sparkle, een intern ontwikkelde AI-agent die nu al ondersteunt bij ticketregistratie, triage, klantvragen en routering. De ambitie is om Sparkle verder te ontwikkelen tot een volwaardige digitale collega die steeds meer operationele processen zelfstandig en betrouwbaar kan uitvoeren. De organisatie kenmerkt zich door korte lijnen, een informele werksfeer en veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief en verantwoordelijkheid. Wat ga je doen? Als Manager Service Operations & AI ben je verantwoordelijk voor de dagelijkse aansturing en verdere professionalisering van de tweedelijns supportorganisatie. Tegelijkertijd speel je een centrale rol in het ontwikkelen en implementeren van AI en automatisering. Je werkzaamheden bestaan uit vier belangrijke onderdelen. Leidinggeven aan de supportorganisatie Je geeft leiding aan een team van 12 tweedelijns supportmedewerkers. Je coacht en ontwikkelt medewerkers en zorgt voor duidelijke prioriteiten, structuur en samenwerking. Je bewaakt de kwaliteit, capaciteit, continuïteit en prestaties van de dienstverlening. Je signaleert knelpunten en vertaalt deze naar concrete verbeteracties. Doorontwikkelen van AI-agent Sparkle Je bent functioneel eigenaar van Sparkle en bepaalt mede de visie, roadmap en prioriteiten. Je vertaalt operationele uitdagingen naar praktische AI-toepassingen. Je zorgt ervoor dat Sparkle veilig, betrouwbaar en gebruiksvriendelijk functioneert. Je werkt samen met technische specialisten aan de verdere ontwikkeling van deze digitale collega. Processen verbeteren en automatiseren Je analyseert bestaande operationele processen en identificeert mogelijkheden voor automatisering. Je optimaliseert workflows, kennisbanken en werkinstructies. Je zorgt voor een goede samenwerking tussen medewerkers en AI. Je draagt bij aan de ambitie om minimaal 75% van de standaard operationele processen met AI te ondersteunen of volledig te automatiseren. Verandering begeleiden Je werkt samen met Operations, Software Development, Business Consultancy en externe partners. Je begeleidt medewerkers in de overgang naar een meer AI-gedreven manier van werken. Je creëert draagvlak, communiceert helder en zorgt ervoor dat veranderingen daadwerkelijk worden doorgevoerd. Wie zoeken wij? Wij zoeken een operationeel sterke manager die structuur weet aan te brengen, medewerkers kan motiveren en tegelijkertijd vooruitkijkt naar de mogelijkheden van nieuwe technologie. Je begrijpt hoe een IT-supportorganisatie werkt, weet hoe je processen beheersbaar en voorspelbaar maakt en krijgt energie van het continu verbeteren van de dienstverlening. Daarnaast beschik je over: Hbo- of wo-werk- en -denkniveau. Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring binnen Managed Services, ICT Operations of IT Service Management. Ervaring met het aansturing, coachen en ontwikkelen van operationele teams. Goede kennis van ITIL-processen en servicemanagement. Affiniteit met AI, automatisering en digitale innovatie. Sterke analytische en organisatorische vaardigheden. Het vermogen om technische mogelijkheden te vertalen naar concrete operationele verbeteringen. Goede communicatieve vaardigheden en ervaring met verandermanagement. Je hoeft geen AI-developer te zijn. We zoeken juist iemand die begrijpt hoe je AI en automatisering succesvol inzet binnen een operationele IT-organisatie en medewerkers hierin weet mee te nemen. Wat kun je verwachten? Je komt rechtstreeks in dienst bij onze opdrachtgever en krijgt een sleutelrol binnen een organisatie die volop investeert in de toekomst van IT-dienstverlening. Je kunt rekenen op: Een bruto maandsalaris van €4.487 tot €6.494, afhankelijk van kennis en ervaring. Een mobiliteitsbudget van €850 per maand, vrij in te zetten op de manier die bij jou past. Een fulltime dienstverband. Flexibele werkmogelijkheden en ruimte om hybride te werken. Veel zelfstandigheid en directe invloed op de ontwikkeling van de organisatie. Ruime mogelijkheden voor persoonlijke en professionele ontwikkeling. De kans om actief bij te dragen aan innovatieve AI- en automatiseringsprojecten. Een informele en professionele werkomgeving met korte lijnen. Een betrokken team van collega's dat samenwerkt aan verbetering en innovatie. Waarom is dit een interessante functie? Wat deze rol bijzonder maakt, is de combinatie van peoplemanagement, operationele verantwoordelijkheid en AI-innovatie. Je krijgt niet alleen de opdracht om een bestaande supportorganisatie goed te laten functioneren, maar ook om deze klaar te maken voor de toekomst. Daarbij krijg je de ruimte om processen structureel te verbeteren, nieuwe technologie toe te passen en daadwerkelijk invloed uit te oefenen op de manier waarop IT-dienstverlening wordt georganiseerd. Een mooie uitdaging voor een ervaren Service Delivery Manager, IT Operations Manager of Support Manager die toe is aan een volgende stap. Interesse? Wil jij leidinggeven aan een IT-supportorganisatie én een belangrijke rol spelen in de verdere ontwikkeling van AI binnen Managed Services? Dan komen wij graag met je in contact! title: Manager Architect Cloud - Paris
description:
Présentation du poste :

Concevoir une architecture d’IA, c’est engager une entreprise pour plusieurs années : l’emplacement des données, la gestion des accès, la manière dont un agent passe en production sous le regard des équipes de sécurité. Ces choix structurants, vous les construisez avec nos clients.

Tout le reste, ce sont les ambitions fonctionnelles et techniques du client, son cadre réglementaire, son budget, les compétences qu'il peut réellement mobiliser en interne, la gouvernance qu'il veut installer, et un écosystème d'éditeurs qui gravite autour de lui. Votre rôle est de trouver le point d'équilibre entre ces forces, de le faire accepter, puis de le réajuster dès que l'une d'elles bouge.

Votre point de départ n’est pas la technologie, mais l’ambition métier. Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.

À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.

Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.

Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, vous rejoignez le département Engineering (environ 300 personnes, sous la responsabilité du CTO), au sein du chapter AI Architect.

Activités et responsabilités :

Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.

Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.

Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT comprennent, et défendre vos choix devant eux.
  • Concevoir des plateformes data et agentiques, on premise, dans le cloud ou en hybride.
  • Découper les périmètres techniques en fonction de la façon dont les équipes du client sont organisées.
  • Arbitrer entre les options en pesant leur valeur métier, leur coût total, leur conformité, leur dépendance à un éditeur et la capacité du client à les faire vivre.
  • Aider le client à évaluer et à mettre en concurrence des éditeurs, sans parti pris.
  • Préparer les propositions commerciales : cadrer la solution, la chiffrer et construire la roadmap de delivery.
  • Tenir la ligne  pendant le delivery : relire les designs, trancher les arbitrages et réajuster la cible quand le contexte du client change.
  • Faire vivre les patterns de référence et les bonnes pratiques du chapter, et suivre de près les évolutions de l’IA, du cloud et de la data.

Profil recherché :

Nous recherchons une personne qui pense comme un consultant et raisonne comme un ingénieur. Les architectes qui réussissent chez nous sont, entre autres, des profils techniques passés par le conseil, des pre-sales engineers, des FDEs, ou des personnes avec une expérience en tant que CTO.

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez conçu une architecture data ou IA qui a été mise en production, et vous savez expliquer pourquoi vous avez écarté les autres options, techniques ou non.
  2. Vous avez déjà recommandé une option techniquement moins séduisante parce qu'elle correspondait mieux au budget, aux compétences, à la gouvernance ou à la réglementation du client.
  3. Vous maîtrisez au moins un grand cloud (Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS) ainsi que les fondamentaux de la sécurité et du réseau : IAM, gestion des secrets, architecture réseau.
  4. Vous avez rédigé des dossiers d’architecture (HLD et LLD) qui ont servi de base à une équipe de delivery.
  5. Vous avez codé pendant une partie significative de votre parcours. Aujourd'hui, vous savez lire du code, challenger un design et dire ce qu'exige un système en production : CI/CD, monitoring, gestion des incidents.
  6. Vous avez déjà cadré et chiffré une solution, par exemple pour une proposition commerciale ou un plan projet.
  7. Vous avez défendu une architecture à la fois devant une direction métier ou un comité de direction, et devant les équipes sécurité et exploitation, en reliant la valeur business, les choix techniques et le plan de delivery.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Architecture de plateformes agentiques : RAG, orchestration multi-agents, choix des technologies couche par couche.
  • Gouvernance des données à l’échelle d’une grande entreprise : data mesh, gestion des accès.
  • Plateformes on premise, hybrides ou souveraines, basées sur des technologies open source ou sur Kubernetes.
  • Standards de run : SLA, PRA et PCA.
  • Une expérience de CTO, de tech lead ou dans un rôle au contact des clients.
  • Une certification d’architecture cloud.
  • Une pratique régulière des coding agents.

Ce poste n'est probablement pas pour vous si votre expertise porte sur une seule plateforme ou un seul éditeur et que vous souhaitez continuer à l'approfondir. Ni si construire et écrire du code est ce qui vous anime le plus : le rôle d'AI Applied Engineer vous correspondra mieux.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Process de recrutement :

  • HR Interview (30-45 min) : Échange sur votre parcours, vos compétences managériales et l'adéquation culturelle avec un Talent Acquisition Specialist.
  • Architecture Case  (60 min) : Session d'architecture avec un AI Architect basé en France sur un cas basé sur une vraie mission.
  • US / Manager Interview (60 min) : Échange avec un Director / Partner pour évaluer le fit managérial, opérationnel et la posture client.

Rémunération : Package :  75 000 € à 85 000 € brut annuel (fixe) + 8 000 € de variable, selon expérience et séniorité.

Présentation de l’entreprise

Artefact est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en data et en intelligence artificielle, qui accompagne les entreprises pour transformer ces technologies en impact business concret et mesurable.

A la croisée du conseil, de la data et de la technologie, nos 2 500 collaborateurs dans 27 pays mettent leurs expertises en commun pour concevoir, développer et déployer des solutions qui répondent aux enjeux de transformation de nos clients.

Envie d'en savoir plus? Découvrez Artefact, nos expertises et notre culture : https://www.artefact.com

 

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l'adéquation avec le rôle.

title: CDI - Senior Platform Engineer - Paris
description:
Mission

Des groupes de premier plan font tourner leur IA sur ce que vous construisez. Infrastructure cloud, plateformes de données, chaînes de delivery, serving de modèles, runtime des agents : ces fondations portent à grande échelle les applications et les agents de nos clients, et vous les concevez et les exploitez. Grâce à ce travail, les équipes produit livrent sans risque, tandis que les coûts, la latence et la sécurité restent sous contrôle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vos utilisateurs sont d’autres équipes d’ingénierie et si la robustesse d’un système sous charge vous intéresse.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Platform Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

Les Product Engineers et les AI Engineers déploient sur les plateformes que vous construisez ; leurs besoins se définissent avec eux, et leur accompagnement se poursuit jusqu’en production.

Sur une plateforme de données, les fondations vous reviennent : infrastructure, sécurité, réseau, calcul. Ce qui y circule relève des Context & Analytics Engineers. Le travail se mène aussi avec les équipes IT, sécurité et cloud du client, sous le regard desquelles chaque choix d’architecture doit pouvoir se défendre ; le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Déployer l’infrastructure cloud en infrastructure as code et conduire les migrations cloud.

  • Construire et exploiter des plateformes de données : entrepôts et lakehouses, orchestration, traitement batch et streaming.

  • Construire des pipelines CI/CD et l’outillage MLOps et LLMOps.

  • Construire le harness des agents : runtime, frameworks d’évaluation, observabilité.

  • Servir les modèles et maîtriser leur coût et leur latence.

  • Poser les fondations de sécurité : IAM, réseau, secrets, droits d’accès des agents, protection contre le prompt injection.

  • Construire des connecteurs et des serveurs MCP que plusieurs agents réutilisent.

  • Garantir la fiabilité : monitoring, gestion des incidents, suivi des coûts.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit et exploité de l’infrastructure cloud sur Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS, en infrastructure as code.

  2. Des pipelines CI/CD et des déploiements conteneurisés, par exemple sur Kubernetes, font partie de votre pratique.

  3. Les bases de la sécurité (IAM, règles réseau, gestion des secrets) s’appliquent chez vous au quotidien.

  4. Ce que vous exploitez, vous le surveillez, et vous prenez part à la gestion des incidents.

  5. Le code et la documentation que vous écrivez restent maintenables pour les équipes qui utilisent votre plateforme.

  6. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de plateformes de données, par exemple sur Databricks, BigQuery ou Snowflake.

  • Une expérience MLOps ou LLMOps : serving de modèles, model registry, pipelines d’évaluation.

  • Une expérience d’observabilité d’agents ou de LLM gateway : tracing, suivi des coûts, routage.

  • FinOps : suivi et optimisation des coûts.

  • Sécurité de l’IA : droits d’accès des agents, red teaming, guardrails.

  • Une certification cloud.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Une plateforme n’est jamais terminée : chaque nouvel agent déployé chez un client soulève de nouvelles questions de coût, de latence et de droits d’accès. Le Platform Engineer travaille à l’endroit où ces questions se posent en premier, au plus près des équipes techniques et de sécurité du client.

Concevoir une architecture d’IA, c’est engager une entreprise pour plusieurs années : l’emplacement des données, la gestion des accès, la manière dont un agent passe en production sous le regard des équipes de sécurité. Ces choix structurants, vous les construisez avec nos clients.

Votre point de départ n’est pas la technologie, mais l’ambition métier. Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.

À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.

Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.

Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. Activités et responsabilités :

Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.

Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.

Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT comprennent, et défendre vos choix devant eux.
  • Concevoir des plateformes data et agentiques, on premise, dans le cloud ou en hybride.
  • Découper les périmètres techniques en fonction de la façon dont les équipes du client sont organisées.
  • Arbitrer entre les options en pesant leur valeur métier, leur coût total, leur conformité, leur dépendance à un éditeur et la capacité du client à les faire vivre.
  • Aider le client à évaluer et à mettre en concurrence des éditeurs, sans parti pris.
  • Préparer les propositions commerciales : cadrer la solution, la chiffrer et construire la roadmap de delivery.
  • Tenir la ligne  pendant le delivery : relire les designs, trancher les arbitrages et réajuster la cible quand le contexte du client change.
  • Faire vivre les patterns de référence et les bonnes pratiques du chapter, et suivre de près les évolutions de l’IA, du cloud et de la data.

Nous recherchons une personne qui pense comme un consultant et raisonne comme un ingénieur. Les architectes qui réussissent chez nous sont, entre autres, des profils techniques passés par le conseil, des pre-sales engineers, des FDEs, ou des personnes avec une expérience en tant que CTO.

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez conçu une architecture data ou IA qui a été mise en production, et vous savez expliquer pourquoi vous avez écarté les autres options, techniques ou non.
  2. Vous avez déjà recommandé une option techniquement moins séduisante parce qu'elle correspondait mieux au budget, aux compétences, à la gouvernance ou à la réglementation du client.
  3. Vous maîtrisez au moins un grand cloud (Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS) ainsi que les fondamentaux de la sécurité et du réseau : IAM, gestion des secrets, architecture réseau.
  4. Vous avez rédigé des dossiers d’architecture (HLD et LLD) qui ont servi de base à une équipe de delivery.
  5. Vous avez codé pendant une partie significative de votre parcours. Aujourd'hui, vous savez lire du code, challenger un design et dire ce qu'exige un système en production : CI/CD, monitoring, gestion des incidents.
  6. Vous avez déjà cadré et chiffré une solution, par exemple pour une proposition commerciale ou un plan projet.
  7. Vous avez défendu une architecture à la fois devant une direction métier ou un comité de direction, et devant les équipes sécurité et exploitation, en reliant la valeur business, les choix techniques et le plan de delivery.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Architecture de plateformes agentiques : RAG, orchestration multi-agents, choix des technologies couche par couche.
  • Gouvernance des données à l’échelle d’une grande entreprise : data mesh, gestion des accès.
  • Plateformes on premise, hybrides ou souveraines, basées sur des technologies open source ou sur Kubernetes.
  • Standards de run : SLA, PRA et PCA.
  • Une expérience de CTO, de tech lead ou dans un rôle au contact des clients.

  • Une pratique régulière des coding agents.

description: About Poesis Whoever builds the leading intelligence for finance will create far more than returns. Poesis is the AI-native investment firm running autonomous agents that predict markets, construct portfolios, and manage risk. Our founders managed institutional capital at Capital Group ($3T AUM) and led enterprise ML at Goldman Sachs and Amazon. We're building a new type of firm, where live capital is the training ground for an intelligence that compounds with every signal. About the Role Financial markets offer something rare in AI research: a continuous, objective feedback loop where you can test new ideas, measure whether they actually work, and use real-world outcomes to inform what you build next. It’s an opportunity to do frontier research with a direct line between the ideas you explore and their real-world performance. As Head of AI, you’ll lead Poesis’s AI strategy and research, setting the technical direction for how we apply frontier AI to investing. You’ll explore new AI approaches, tackle difficult research problems and help define how we use AI to better understand and predict financial markets. This is a hands-on leadership role where you’ll set the research agenda while continuing to work directly on technical challenges. Challenges You’ll Work On Set Poesis’s AI research direction, identify the hardest problems worth solving and guide the team's technical work. Push the capabilities of foundation models, agentic systems and world models through new architectures and research approaches. Explore pre-training, mid-training and post-training methods to improve how models learn, reason and adapt. Advance tabular ML research, including emerging methods such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs). Tackle the challenges of learning from small, high-dimensional datasets where traditional ML methods struggle. Turn promising research into models and systems that can solve difficult real-world problems. About You You’ve done exceptional AI research at a frontier AI lab, leading research initiatives and helping set technical direction. You have deep expertise in modern AI architectures, model training and machine learning. You have a strong research track record, including relevant publications. You have strong mathematical and statistical foundations and know how to tackle difficult problems with limited, complex data. You’re a hands-on technical leader who can guide other researchers while developing, testing and implementing your own ideas. Nice to Have Experience with frontier tabular ML methods. Experience applying ML to financial markets or complex, high-dimensional datasets. Location Hybrid, 3 days per week on-site at our office in Menlo Park, CA, London, or Zurich. Relocation allowance available. Compensation Competitive cash compensation commensurate with experience, plus equity and carry (share of fund profits). Benefits We offer excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage, alongside a strong benefits package that includes catered lunches, commuter benefits, and more. For U.S. candidates, current legal authorization to work in the US required; continuing work visa sponsorship available for full-time employees. Working at Poesis As an early team member, you’ll help shape not just the product, but how the company operates. Your decisions will have lasting impact across the business. title: QA Engineer
description: About Neuroscale AI Neuroscale AI is building a next-generation AI recruiting and talent intelligence platform that helps organizations turn hiring into a measurable, repeatable, and intelligent science. Our ARBI platform supports sourcing, screening, evaluation, sequencing, scheduling, recruiter workflow automation, and explainable candidate assessment for commercial enterprises, public-sector agencies, higher education, staffing organizations, and workforce-development teams. Neuroscale is also building Athena, an AI-powered career readiness and candidate-assistance experience that helps users improve resumes, prepare for interviews, receive rubric-based feedback, and navigate the job search process with personalized AI support. We are a fast-moving startup operating at the intersection of GenAI, HR technology, recruiting operations, career services, workflow automation, and enterprise AI deployment. As ARBI and Athena scale across customers, we need a senior quality leader who can make product quality measurable, automated, auditable, and trusted. Role Overview We are hiring a Senior QA Engineer / Quality Engineering Lead to own quality assurance, testing strategy, product validation, and release readiness across ARBI and Athena. This is a hands-on senior role for someone who can test deeply, build automated quality systems, validate AI workflows, improve developer quality practices, and become the central authority for product quality. This role is not limited to executing test cases. You will audit the current QA landscape, define the testing strategy, build regression and automation frameworks, validate AI behavior, pressure-test edge cases, and create the release confidence needed for a rapidly evolving SaaS platform. You will work closely with engineering, product, design, customer success, and founders to make sure new features, bug fixes, experiments, integrations, data workflows, and AI-driven experiences ship with clarity, reliability, auditability, accessibility, and user trust. What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities) 1) Build the Quality Strategy and QA Operating System • Perform a deep audit of the current QA setup across ARBI, Athena, frontend flows, backend services, APIs, data workflows, integrations, AI pipelines, and release processes. • Define a company-wide QA strategy across short-term stabilization, mid-term automation, and long-term quality engineering maturity. • Design a scalable test architecture using test pyramid principles, shift-left testing, smoke testing, regression testing, release gates, exploratory testing, and risk-based coverage. • Define clear QA responsibilities between developers, QA, product, design, customer success, and release owners. • Establish a practical quality operating rhythm: test plans, release checklists, defect triage, severity definitions, sign-off workflows, and quality metrics. 2) Own Product QA for ARBI and Athena • Validate implementation against requirements, designs, copy, acceptance criteria, user stories, and customer-specific workflows. • Test UI, UX, business logic, responsiveness, edge cases, error states, empty states, loading states, accessibility, and validation messages. • Perform exploratory, smoke, regression, and release-candidate testing before launches. • Validate recruiter workflows including candidate search, matching, scoring, resume parsing, outreach sequencing, scheduling, recruiter dashboards, candidate profiles, and ATS/CRM-style workflows. • Validate Athena workflows including resume support, interview preparation, rubric-based feedback, candidate assistance, AI-generated recommendations, and user-facing guidance. 3) Build and Modernize Test Automation • Take ownership of automated frontend, API, integration, and end-to-end test coverage using Cypress, Playwright, Pytest, Postman/Newman, or equivalent tools. • Create reliable automated regression suites for critical ARBI and Athena workflows, including authentication, permissions, candidate pipelines, analytics, notifications, integrations, and admin experiences. • Integrate tests deeply into CI/CD pipelines so failures are visible, actionable, and tied to release confidence. • Improve test reliability, execution speed, data setup, fixture management, and maintainability. • Introduce AI-assisted testing practices where useful, while maintaining clear human judgment and repeatable test evidence. 4) Validate Backend, API, Data, and Workflow Reliability • Test robust REST APIs, Python/FastAPI services, backend business logic, asynchronous workflows, and data-processing pipelines. • Validate PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenSearch, Celery, Temporal, containerized services, deployment pipelines, and AWS-hosted environments from a QA perspective. • Create API and integration test coverage for imports, exports, webhooks, permissions, search, scoring, candidate data, customer-specific configuration, and workflow automation. • Test with realistic and large-scale datasets to uncover performance, latency, search relevance, data integrity, and resilience issues. • Establish baseline performance, load, and reliability testing using JMeter, k6, Locust, or similar tools. 5) QA AI, LLM, and Evaluation Workflows • Validate AI-assisted recruiting workflows for accuracy, consistency, explainability, hallucination risk, bias risk, prompt adherence, rubric alignment, and human-in-the-loop behavior. • Test AI scoring, candidate summaries, recommendations, interview feedback, resume analysis, and knowledge-retrieval experiences across normal, adversarial, and edge-case inputs. • Create repeatable evaluation datasets and test harnesses to measure AI quality over time. • Validate guardrails, fallback behavior, citations, confidence indicators, data boundaries, audit trails, and customer-specific configuration. • Partner with product and engineering to define what “good” means for AI-generated outputs and how release readiness should be measured. 6) Own Release Readiness and Quality Visibility • Create clear, structured, reproducible bug reports with screenshots/videos, environment details, severity, expected behavior, actual behavior, impact, and reproduction steps. • Retest fixed issues, validate root-cause resolution, and prevent regressions. • Communicate QA status clearly before release: passed, failed, blocked, passed with known issues, or requires founder/product decision. • Build dashboards and reporting for test coverage, defect trends, regression health, release risk, performance baselines, and customer-impacting quality issues. • Help developers produce testable, high-quality code by establishing testing standards, review practices, and shared quality expectations. What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months) • A clear QA audit, quality strategy, and implementation roadmap are delivered and accepted by engineering and product leadership. • A comprehensive ARBI and Athena test case portfolio exists across critical user journeys, backend services, data workflows, AI behavior, integrations, and release gates. • Automated test coverage increases meaningfully across the highest-risk frontend, API, integration, and regression areas. • CI/CD quality gates are established so test results directly inform release decisions. • Baseline performance, load, security-oriented, and resilience testing practices are introduced for critical workflows. • Release readiness becomes transparent, repeatable, and trusted by founders, engineering, product, customer success, and customers. • You become the central authority for product quality and a mentor to developers on testing best practices. Preferred Qualifications • Prior experience as a Staff QA Engineer, Lead QA Engineer, Quality Engineering Lead, SDET Lead, Founding QA Engineer, or QA Architect. • Experience testing AI/LLM products, evaluation workflows, RAG systems, AI copilots, agentic workflows, or human-in-the-loop decision systems. • Experience in HR tech, recruiting platforms, ATS/CRM systems, career services, assessment platforms, or workforce development products. • Experience with A/B testing, feature flags, analytics validation, event tracking, access control, subscription/billing flows, or customer-specific configurations. • Experience with performance and load testing tools such as JMeter, k6, Locust, or similar platforms. • Familiarity with security, privacy, accessibility, SOC 2-style controls, federal deployment expectations, or auditability requirements. • Comfort working directly with founders, customers, customer success, and implementation teams to translate real-world feedback into quality improvements. Current / Target Tech Environment • Frontend: ReactJS / modern web application interfaces. • Backend: Python, FastAPI, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Redis, OpenSearch, Celery, Temporal, and asynchronous workflow services. • Infrastructure: AWS, Docker, containers, CI/CD pipelines, observability tooling, and production SaaS deployment practices. • Testing: Cypress / Playwright-style E2E testing, API testing, integration testing, regression suites, performance testing, and AI-assisted QA workflows. Compensation & Benefits • Base Salary: Competitive and commensurate with experience, seniority, location, and ability to own quality across the product. • Performance / Equity: Potential performance incentives and/or equity participation based on final offer structure. • Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, PTO, and company-supported professional growth. • Learning: Support for relevant courses, conferences, certifications, technical books, and quality engineering communities. • Flexibility: Remote-first / hybrid flexibility with strong preference for Northern VA / DC-area alignment and occasional in-person collaboration. Equal Opportunity Neuroscale is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

raw.jobDescription:
This role may require in-person interview/s in Austin, Texas

About Osano:

Osano is an innovative B-Corporation built around a simple belief: privacy is a fundamental right. Since day one, we’ve been focused on giving modern enterprises the ability to innovate quickly, stay competitive, and earn customer trust by respecting data privacy and complying with consent guidelines. Our products help organizations operate confidently in a rapidly evolving regulatory and technological landscape.

About The Role:

We're looking for a product-minded Senior Software Engineer to own meaningful parts of the Osano platform end to end, from shaping a problem with Product to running the result in production.

This role is for an engineer who treats AI tooling as a real force multiplier. You use coding agents and AI-assisted workflows to explore unfamiliar code faster, ship more and remove repetitive work. You also have the judgment to verify everything that goes out under your name. We want someone whose impact goes beyond what they write by hand, and who helps the engineers around them do the same.

You'll work across our React front end, Node.js services, PostgreSQL data stores and AWS infrastructure. You'll partner closely with Product, Design, QA and Security.

This is a remote role. You must be based in, and authorized to work in, the United States.

What you'll do:

Build and ship product, end to end

  • Lead multi-sprint projects from design through rollout: turn a loosely defined problem into a plan, break it into work that you and others can action, and deliver close to estimate.
  • Design systems that hold up, and write design docs and decision records that weigh the alternatives.
  • Partner with Product on scope: propose MVP cuts, phasing and tradeoffs, and measure whether what we shipped actually helped customers.

Engineer with AI to multiply your impact

  • Use AI coding agents and assistants across the whole development lifecycle: exploring codebases, scaffolding, writing tests, debugging, refactoring, migrations and code review.
  • Stay accountable for every line you ship. You understand and can explain AI-generated code, and you know where AI shouldn't be trusted.
  • Turn repetitive engineering work into automation: scripts, agent workflows, and checks that save your team time every week.
  • Share what works: help define how our teams use AI tools, and how we review and verify AI-assisted work.
  • Use AI responsibly. Customer and personal data stays out of AI tools except through approved, privacy-safe paths. This is non-negotiable at a privacy company.

Own what you ship in production

  • Build observability, feature flags and rollback paths into your work from the start.
  • Take turns on our triage and on-call rotation. Lead incident response for your team's systems, and see postmortem follow-ups through to completion.
  • Identify tech debt, size it, and make the case to get it into the plan.

Build with privacy and security by design

  • Apply data minimization, residency, retention and access controls to the systems you design, especially those that handle customer and personal data.
  • Write secure code and fix vulnerabilities in your area as part of normal work.

Raise the bar and grow others

  • Give code and design reviews that change outcomes, not just approvals.
  • Mentor engineers earlier in their careers, and make your team better at testing, reviewing and operating software.
  • Interview candidates and help us hire well.

About you:

  • Delightful Experience. You care about the customer problem, not just the ticket, and you push for what actually helps.
  • Own Your Impact. You take full responsibility for outcomes, from the first design doc to how the feature behaves in production at 2 a.m.
  • Stronger Together. You put team success ahead of individual wins, give direct and kind feedback, and treat documentation and async communication as first-class work.
  • Growth Mindset. You're curious and keep learning, especially as AI changes how software gets built. You're excited about what it can do without overselling it or ignoring its limits.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity and create clarity for others through good design and clear writing.

Must-haves:

  • Typically 5+ years building and shipping production software. We care more about what you've owned than the number of years.
  • A track record of leading multi-sprint projects from design to production in a team setting.
  • Strong JavaScript/Node.js and React experience, and solid relational database skills (PostgreSQL preferred).
  • Strong system design fundamentals: data modeling, API design, and naming the tradeoffs.
  • Experience owning production systems: on-call, incident response, observability.
  • Hands-on, day-to-day use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot, with concrete examples of how they made you or your team more effective, and how you verify their output.
  • Experience mentoring other engineers.
  • Strong written communication in a remote, async environment.

Nice-to-haves:

  • AWS experience (ECS/Fargate, Lambda, S3, RDS), especially multi-region or data-residency work.
  • Privacy, security or compliance-sensitive B2B SaaS (GDPR, CCPA, SOC 2).
  • Building AI-powered automations, agent workflows or LLM-based product features.
  • Data and analytics tooling (Redshift, Athena) or event-driven architectures.
  • CI/CD, preview/ephemeral environments, end-to-end testing (Cypress).

How we work:

  • Fully remote, with at least four hours of overlap each day with your team's core hours.
  • Collaborative and video-on for meetings, and async-first for everything else. Bring people in when they are needed and share what you’re working on with the team.
  • Regular 1:1 checkins with your manager, with a focus on growth conversations.

Why Us:

  • We're a welcoming team that's dependable, curious, moves fast, and full of talented people
  • We're a B-corporation with a mission that matters, in a high-growth space with significant potential
  • You'll have access to our training program, well-defined career paths, and a leadership team that values professional development

Benefits:

  • Competitive-pay compensation and ownership interest/equity
  • Unlimited paid time off, plus a requirement to take at least two weeks off per year
  • We're a Best Place for Working Parents and offer paid parental leave for all new parents
  • Osano sponsors individual premiums on base plans at 100% and dependent premiums at 50% for Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance via Aetna
  • A fully and permanently remote company, so you can work from anywhere in the U.S.
  • Receive a MacBook and $600 to craft your home workspace
  • Annual company trip designed to foster connection, creativity, and fun
  • Mental health benefits with free memberships to mindfulness and talk therapy services

A Bit More About Osano:

Osano is a leading data privacy platform that helps organizations quickly and confidently comply with laws like GDPR, CCPA, and other global privacy regulations. From consent management to vendor risk monitoring, Osano makes complex privacy tasks refreshingly simple, so companies can focus on what they do best, while we handle the rest.

We’re backed by top-tier investors, including Baird Capital, Jump Capital, and LiveOak, and we’re scaling fast with a multi-year runway and ambitious growth plans. We’ve also been recognized as a Great Place to Work for four years running, with 97% of employees saying Osano is a great place to work.

Osano is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer - Singapore
description: Who We Are Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too. We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s computer vision AI open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety , digitizing floor plans , preserving coral reef populations , guiding drone flight , and much more . Roboflow is supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Y Combinator, Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors. Roboflowers are passionate builders who value ownership, accountability, and a bias toward action. We’re curious, hands-on with new tech, and prefer showing our work over talking about it. Many of us have a founder mindset and thrive in our high-autonomy environment. What You’ll Do We’re hiring Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) to be the first technical hands on our new customer’s Roboflow deployments. After our Sales and Solutions Architecture team closes a deal and validates the technical approach, you step in to take it from proof-of-concept to production, the critical 0-to-1 phase where vision meets reality. You’ll embed directly with new Customers, working alongside their engineering and operations teams to build and deploy their first production computer vision workflows on Roboflow. This is the most difficult, important and rewarding phase of the customer journey. Infrastructure is unfamiliar, data pipelines need to be built, edge devices need to be configured, and models need to perform in real-world conditions, not just in a demo or a lab. The FDE role is more than just execution, you are also our eyes and ears in the field. You'll see the gap between what a Customer thinks they want, and what they actually need. That insight is invaluable, and you'll feed it directly back to our Product and Engineering teams, shaping the Roboflow platform and solution offerings. The best FDEs don't just deploy solutions; they surface the problems worth solving next. Once you’ve proven the deployment works in production and the customer’s team is equipped to operate it, you hand off to our Implementation Engineers who scale, optimize, and expand the solution across additional use cases. You’re the tip of the spear, the person who makes the first deployment work, no matter what it takes; the adventurer, the explorer, the builder. Five years from now, FDE at Roboflow on a resume should mean what a few years at Palantir or a FAANG company means. That's the bar we're hiring against. Role and Responsibilities 0-to-1 Deployment: Take validated proof-of-concepts from the pre-sales process and build the first production deployment. This includes data pipeline setup, model optimization, edge device configuration, and integration with customer infrastructure. Edge-First Engineering: Deploy and operate computer vision systems on edge hardware in physical environments. Where conditions are unpredictable and connectivity is unreliable. This is hands-on, hardware-heavy work. Embed with Customers: Work on-site or deeply embedded with the customer’s engineering team during the initial deployment phase (typically 4–12 weeks per engagement). Build trust, transfer knowledge, and establish the foundation for long-term success. Production Engineering: Write production-grade code that will live in the customer’s environment. Handle the messy realities of real-world computer vision: lighting variability, camera calibration, model drift, network latency, and edge hardware constraints. Be Our Eyes and Ears in the Field: You'll be closer to the customer's real problems than anyone else at Roboflow. You'll surface the gap between what the customer says they want, what they actually need, and what the machine operators on the floor think. That feedback loop back to Product and Engineering shapes what we build next, and it's one of the most valuable things FDEs bring back to the company. Knowledge Transfer & Handoff: Document your deployment architecture, create runbooks, and train the customer’s team so they can operate the system independently. Provide a clean handoff to Roboflow’s Implementation Engineers for scaling and expansion. De-risk New Deployments: Identify and resolve technical risks early. If a customer’s environment won’t support the planned architecture, you find the alternative before it becomes a project failure. raw.jobDescription:
Who We Are

Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too.

We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s computer vision AI open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety, digitizing floor plans, preserving coral reef populations, guiding drone flight, and much more.

Roboflow is supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Y Combinator, Google Ventures, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors.

Roboflowers are passionate builders who value ownership, accountability, and a bias toward action. We’re curious, hands-on with new tech, and prefer showing our work over talking about it. Many of us have a founder mindset and thrive in our high-autonomy environment.

What You’ll Do

We’re hiring Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) to be the first technical hands on our new customer’s Roboflow deployments. After our Sales and Solutions Architecture team closes a deal and validates the technical approach, you step in to take it from proof-of-concept to production, the critical 0-to-1 phase where vision meets reality.

You’ll embed directly with new Customers, working alongside their engineering and operations teams to build and deploy their first production computer vision workflows on Roboflow. This is the most difficult, important and rewarding phase of the customer journey. Infrastructure is unfamiliar, data pipelines need to be built, edge devices need to be configured, and models need to perform in real-world conditions, not just in a demo or a lab.

The FDE role is more than just execution, you are also our eyes and ears in the field. You'll see the gap between what a Customer thinks they want, and what they actually need. That insight is invaluable, and you'll feed it directly back to our Product and Engineering teams, shaping the Roboflow platform and solution offerings. The best FDEs don't just deploy solutions; they surface the problems worth solving next.

Once you’ve proven the deployment works in production and the customer’s team is equipped to operate it, you hand off to our Implementation Engineers who scale, optimize, and expand the solution across additional use cases. You’re the tip of the spear, the person who makes the first deployment work, no matter what it takes; the adventurer, the explorer, the builder.

Five years from now, FDE at Roboflow on a resume should mean what a few years at Palantir or a FAANG company means. That's the bar we're hiring against.

Role and Responsibilities

  • 0-to-1 Deployment: Take validated proof-of-concepts from the pre-sales process and build the first production deployment. This includes data pipeline setup, model optimization, edge device configuration, and integration with customer infrastructure.

  • Edge-First Engineering: Deploy and operate computer vision systems on edge hardware in physical environments. Where conditions are unpredictable and connectivity is unreliable. This is hands-on, hardware-heavy work.

  • Embed with Customers: Work on-site or deeply embedded with the customer’s engineering team during the initial deployment phase (typically 4–12 weeks per engagement). Build trust, transfer knowledge, and establish the foundation for long-term success.

  • Production Engineering: Write production-grade code that will live in the customer’s environment. Handle the messy realities of real-world computer vision: lighting variability, camera calibration, model drift, network latency, and edge hardware constraints.

  • Be Our Eyes and Ears in the Field: You'll be closer to the customer's real problems than anyone else at Roboflow. You'll surface the gap between what the customer says they want, what they actually need, and what the machine operators on the floor think. That feedback loop back to Product and Engineering shapes what we build next, and it's one of the most valuable things FDEs bring back to the company.

  • Knowledge Transfer & Handoff: Document your deployment architecture, create runbooks, and train the customer’s team so they can operate the system independently. Provide a clean handoff to Roboflow’s Implementation Engineers for scaling and expansion.

  • De-risk New Deployments: Identify and resolve technical risks early. If a customer’s environment won’t support the planned architecture, you find the alternative before it becomes a project failure.

  • Shape the Deployment Playbook: Codify repeatable deployment patterns, starter templates, and reusable artifacts that make future deployments faster and more reliable.

The Skillset You’ll Bring

  • Meaningful experience deploying technology in physical-world environments. We value breadth, working across different industries, hardware platforms, and deployment contexts, over depth at a single company. The best FDEs we've hired have built things in factories, warehouses, construction sites, or labs before ever touching a vision model.

  • Strong proficiency in Python; experience with systems-level work (Docker, Kubernetes, networking, Linux) is highly valued.

  • Hands-on experience deploying machine learning or computer vision models to production; you understand the gap between a working notebook and a reliable pipeline.

  • Experience with edge computing hardware and constraints (NVIDIA Jetson, industrial cameras, limited connectivity, on-premise security requirements).

  • Excellent troubleshooting and debugging skills; you’re the person who figures out why it works in staging but not in production.

  • Strong interpersonal skills - you'll be embedded with customer teams and need to build trust quickly while navigating their internal dynamics. You'll talk to executives, engineers, and machine operators, sometimes in the same meeting.

  • Experience in one or more of Roboflow’s target verticals: manufacturing, logistics, food processing, automotive, or retail.

  • Willingness to travel ~40–50% for on-site customer deployments.

Preferred Attributes

  • Experience in a professional services, deployment engineering, or forward deployed engineering role.

  • Familiarity with CV/MLOps tooling and practices (model versioning, monitoring, retraining pipelines).

  • Deep industrial subject matter expertise. The kind of person who can walk onto a production line and immediately start asking the right questions about throughput, defect rates, and inspection points.

  • Background in IoT, embedded systems, or infrastructure engineering alongside hands-on deployment experience.

  • You're a tinkerer outside of work. You own a 3D printer, you've got Raspberry Pis running something in your house, you're constantly tweaking your home network or smart home setup. You enjoy figuring out why something doesn't work as much as you enjoy building it in the first place.

Who You’ll Be Working With

Our team of ~120 attracts talent like executives that wanted to return to building, founders with a 100M+ exit, Roboflow users turned team members, open source contributors, a cyclist who biked across the United States, prolific high school hackers, a CTO from 100+ engineering organization, amongst many exceptional others.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll be partnering directly with our co-founder/CEO and Sales leadership to not only do great work in the role, but shape how this function works for the future of Roboflow.

Where You’ll Work

This role is based in Singapore. You’ll be part of a distributed team that works closely across time zones, with regular opportunities to get together in person (like team onsites in different cities) and a $4000 USD/yr travel stipend to make those trips happen. Work from home, from a co-working space, or wherever you do your best work. We want you to work where you work best!

When You’ll Work

Roboflow’s core team is largely US-based, so you’ll have a small number of synchronous meetings each week that fall outside standard Singapore hours (typically early morning or evening SGT). Beyond that, your schedule follows your customers and your deployments, and we work asynchronously with the rest of the team.

What You’ll Receive

To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every six months to ensure we stay in line with the market.

In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits:

  • $4000/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers

  • $350/mo Productivity stipend to spend on things that make your work environment more productive, like high-speed internet at home or a co-working space

  • $350/mo AI Tools

  • $150/mo Team lunch

  • $500/one time Home office

  • Equity in the company so we are all invested in the future of computer vision

Interview Process (~5 hours)

Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. We are all motivated to work with an exceptional team, who you’ll be speaking directly with about what it’s like to work and thrive at Roboflow. We like to be decisive and work fast, so don’t be surprised if all the below conversations happen over a few days.

Before the Interview:

  • We’ll review your application, LinkedIn, Github, etc.

  • The best way to stand out is to write about something you’ve built with Roboflow or contribute to one of our open source projects.

  • We may send you a technical screen if applicable.

Introduction Phase:

  • [45m] Meet with hiring manager to assess for overall mindset and skillset

Team Interview Phase:

  • [60m] Technical Assessment - live coding or architecture session

  • [30m] Demo - build a project with Roboflow and share your work

Final Interview Stage:

  • [30m] Meet with Head of Operations, for a culture discussion

  • [30m] Meet with Joseph Nelson, CEO

Note: you are welcome to request additional conversations with anyone you would like to meet and we will accommodate as best we can.

Not Sure If This Is You?

We want a diverse, global team with a broad range of experience and perspectives. If this job sounds great, but you’re not sure if you qualify, look into our Former Founders role or subscribe to our career newsletter by emailing “Subscribe” to operations@roboflow.com. We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

Learn More About Us

We are building a diverse Distributed team that is distributed across the globe. Roboflow is an equal opportunity workplace; we welcome people from all backgrounds, communities, and experiences.

We provide competitive compensation and stellar benefits to accelerate your personal and work life. Learn more about what it is like to work at Roboflow by reading these blog posts.

Equal Employment Opportunity

At Roboflow, we believe great ideas come from everywhere, and everyone. We’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

title: Senior Reliability Engineer
description: About Halter At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures . To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram . About the role We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. We can’t wait a decade to find out whether a design will survive - so we have to know before it ships. That’s the job of our Reliability team. As a Reliability Engineer, you’ll be the person who turns “it needs to last” into evidence. You’ll own reliability for products and subsystems through development: assessing risk early, designing accelerated tests grounded in physics of failure, building the models that link hours in a chamber to years on a cow, and making a clear, evidence-backed call on whether a design is ready. You’ll close the loop with the field, comparing what fails out there with what our testing predicted, and changing our tests where they missed. What you’ll do Own the reliability plan for a product or major subsystem through development - turning reliability goals into measurable requirements, test plans and acceptance criteria Lead risk assessments, including failure mode and effects analysis and fault tree analysis, and review designs for robustness alongside mechanical, electrical and firmware engineers Design and run accelerated tests, including highly accelerated life testing and accelerated life testing, built from first principles and physics of failure, with clear learning goals and decision criteria Build reliability and acceleration models that link test time to field life, and write scripts and tools to automate repeated data analysis Correlate field failures with test results - show where our testing caught a failure mode, flag where it didn’t, and develop new test methods to replicate the field stresses we’re missing Write reliability reports and sign-off recommendations that others can audit, with residual risk and the evidence behind it made clear Assess the reliability impact of design, component, production and supplier changes, and work with suppliers on component qualification Improve our lab capability - evaluating and introducing new test equipment, fixtures and methods, and scoping and reviewing work from external labs Mentor and support junior engineers, reviewing their test setups and data and explaining the reasoning behind our methods This is a hands-on, first-principles role. We're looking for someone with real experience in reliability or hardware test engineering who wants to go deep on the craft - and who will hold the line on an unwelcome conclusion when the evidence supports it. We’re open on level and will work out the right fit through the interview process, from an experienced individual contributor through to someone ready to set technical direction for the team. What you’ll bring Several years of experience in reliability, test or hardware engineering on electronic or electromechanical products - a degree in electrical, mechanical, mechatronics or materials engineering, or similar, is preferred Hands-on experience designing and running reliability tests, such as accelerated life testing, highly accelerated life testing, or environmental and mechanical stress testing A solid understanding of how electronic products fail - for example solder joint fatigue, corrosion, moisture ingress, battery degradation and connector wear - and the physics that drives them Confidence with reliability statistics and modelling, such as life data analysis, acceleration models, confidence levels and sample sizing A first-principles mindset - you want to understand why a test represents the field, not just that it follows a standard Clear, honest communication grounded in evidence. You can explain risk and uncertainty to people outside your discipline, and you’ll hold your ground on an unwelcome conclusion when the data backs it Strong sense of ownership and a bias for action - you see what needs doing and get on with it without waiting to be asked A tenacious curiosity to figure things out, and the process discipline to do it properly every time Low ego, highly collaborative and willing to play for the front of the Jersey. Join our team Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit! If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch! Please also feel free to check out the careers page for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn & Instagram . Why our team loves working at Halter: Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations. Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems. You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our personal growth fund. This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

About the role

We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. We can’t wait a decade to find out whether a design will survive - so we have to know before it ships. That’s the job of our Reliability team.

  • Own the reliability plan for a product or major subsystem through development - turning reliability goals into measurable requirements, test plans and acceptance criteria

  • Mentor and support junior engineers, reviewing their test setups and data and explaining the reasoning behind our methods

  • A first-principles mindset - you want to understand why a test represents the field, not just that it follows a standard

  • Strong sense of ownership and a bias for action - you see what needs doing and get on with it without waiting to be asked

title: Senior Director, Head of Quality & Responsible Person, International
description:
Mavericks Wanted 

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on 
 
In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. We build bridges to groundbreaking advancements in rare disease, and develop life-changing medicines for patients with unmet needs as fast as humanly possible.  
 
Together we define white space, push boundaries, and empower people to solve problems. If you're someone who defies convention, join us and work alongside some of the most respected minds in the industry. Together, we'll ask "why not?" and help reengineer the future of biopharma. At BridgeBio, we value curiosity and experimentation—including the ethical & thoughtful use of AI to improve clarity, speed, and quality of work. 

What You’ll Do

The Sr Director, Head of Quality & Responsible Person, International, leads quality for infigratinib, and will be the designated Responsible Person on the entity's wholesale distribution authorisation. The role reports to the Head of Quality, QED, with a dotted line to local managing director, and is based in the Netherlands. If the entity becomes the marketing authorisation holder for infigratinib, the role also covers the related MAH quality duties. The role holds an unrestricted right of escalation to the entity's full board and is independent of commercial operations and of manufacturing/supply with EU-GDP guidelines, relevant EU directives (including the Falsified Medicines Directive), Dutch Medicines Act, and public service requirements. This role acts as a QA liaison of BridgeBio's contract service providers (CSPs), providing oversight of lot release activities. This role includes reviewing and approving batch records, certificates of analysis, and compliance documents, providing quality review of deviations, change controls, and CAPAs related to assigned CSPs, collaborating closely with CSPs and internal teams such as quality control, manufacturing, regulatory affairs, and supply chain. The role builds and leads a small quality team (deputy RP, QA compliance/QMS, QA operations/GDP), owns the quality management system across the Skeletal Dysplasia assets, and leads WDA licensing, inspection readiness and potentially subsequent MIA readiness, if needed in the future.

Responsibilities

Major Responsibilities / Accountabilities

  • Serve as the named Responsible Person on the WDA: release for distribution, recall decisions, and GDP compliance of the entity
  • Leads and develops the entity's quality team: deputy RP, QA compliance/QMS, and QA operations/GDP; and QP
